html:
The First Chimurenga was the rising of the Ndebele and Shona against the rule of the British South Africa Company in 1896 and 1897, known to the British as the Second Matabele War.

The Ndebele rose in March 1896 after drought, cattle disease and forced labour, and the Shona, who had not been expected to fight, rose in June. Hundreds of settlers were killed. Spirit mediums such as Nehanda and Kaguvi helped inspire and organise the rising.

Company and British troops crushed it by 1897, dynamiting caves where people hid, and the mediums were hanged in 1898. Nehanda's last words were remembered as a prophecy that her bones would rise again. The guerrillas of the Bush War called their struggle the Second Chimurenga, after this rising against settler rule in Zimbabwe.
